\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering
\caption{Cross sections for inclusive production of positively charged hadrons ($h^+$) in deep-inelastic scattering, for the kinematic region $150.0 < Q^2 < 300.0$~GeV$^2$ and $0.0021 \leq x < 0.0071$, tabulated in bins of the hadron energy fraction $z$ and the hadron transverse momentum $p_{T,h}$. The selection requires $Q^2 > 150$~GeV$^2$; only hadrons within the central tracking region, $|\eta_h| < 1.6$, are included. The tabulated entries are cross sections divided by the bin volume in $Q^2$, $x$, $z$ and $p_{T,h}$, in units of nb~GeV$^{-3}$; the bin volume is given in the last column of the table, and the entries are a derived view of the tabulated integrated cross sections. For the bins whose upper $x$ edge lies above $1$, only the range up to $x = 1$ enters the bin volume. The values are Born-level cross sections: they are corrected for detector effects and for radiative (QED and electroweak) effects; the correction convention is photon exchange only, i.e. the cross sections are defined without $Z$-boson exchange. Each cross section is quoted with its statistical uncertainty and its total systematic uncertainty. Two correction factors are tabulated for reference: the factor applied in this table (seventh column), which follows the photon-exchange-only convention, and the corresponding factor of the convention with $Z$-boson exchange included (sixth column); the ratio of the two factors converts a cross section between the two conventions. The values are preliminary and subject to change.}

The selection requires $Q^2 > 150$~GeV$^2$; only hadrons within the central tracking region, $|\eta_h| < 1.6$, are included. The tabulated entries are cross sections divided by the bin volume in $Q^2$, $x$, $z$ and $p_{T,h}$, in units of nb~GeV$^{-3}$; the bin volume is given in the last column of the table, and the entries are a derived view of the tabulated integrated cross sections. For the bins whose upper $x$ edge lies above $1$, only the range up to $x = 1$ enters the bin volume. The values are Born-level cross sections: they are corrected for detector effects and for radiative (QED and electroweak) effects; the correction convention is photon exchange only, i.e. the cross sections are defined without $Z$-boson exchange. Each cross section is quoted with its statistical uncertainty and its total systematic uncertainty. Two correction factors are tabulated for reference: the factor applied in this table (seventh column), which follows the photon-exchange-only convention, and the corresponding factor of the convention with $Z$-boson exchange included (sixth column); the ratio of the two factors converts a cross section between the two conventions. The selection requires $Q^2 > 150$~GeV$^2$; only hadrons within the central tracking region, $|\eta_h| < 1.6$, are included. The tabulated entries are cross sections divided by the bin volume in $Q^2$, $x$, $z$ and $p_{T,h}$, in units of nb~GeV$^{-3}$; the bin volume is given in the last column of the table, and the entries are a derived view of the tabulated integrated cross sections. For the bins whose upper $x$ edge lies above $1$, only the range up to $x = 1$ enters the bin volume. The values are Born-level cross sections: they are corrected for detector effects and for radiative (QED and electroweak) effects; the correction convention is photon exchange only, i.e. the cross sections are defined without $Z$-boson exchange. Each cross section is quoted with its statistical uncertainty and its total systematic uncertainty. Two correction factors are tabulated for reference: the factor applied in this table (seventh column), which follows the photon-exchange-only convention, and the corresponding factor of the convention with $Z$-boson exchange included (sixth column); the ratio of the two factors converts a cross section between the two conventions. The values are preliminary and subject to change.}

For the bins whose upper $x$ edge lies above $1$, only the range up to $x = 1$ enters the bin volume. The values are Born-level cross sections: they are corrected for detector effects and for radiative (QED and electroweak) effects; the correction convention is photon exchange only, i.e. the cross sections are defined without $Z$-boson exchange. Each cross section is quoted with its statistical uncertainty and its total systematic uncertainty. Two correction factors are tabulated for reference: the factor applied in this table (seventh column), which follows the photon-exchange-only convention, and the corresponding factor of the convention with $Z$-boson exchange included (sixth column); the ratio of the two factors converts a cross section between the two conventions. Each cross section is quoted with its statistical uncertainty and its total systematic uncertainty. Two correction factors are tabulated for reference: the factor applied in this table (seventh column), which follows the photon-exchange-only convention, and the corresponding factor of the convention with $Z$-boson exchange included (sixth column); the ratio of the two factors converts a cross section between the two conventions. The selection requires $Q^2 > 150$~GeV$^2$; only hadrons within the central tracking region, $|\eta_h| < 1.6$, are included. The tabulated entries are cross sections divided by the bin volume in $Q^2$, $x$, $z$ and $p_{T,h}$, in units of nb~GeV$^{-3}$; the bin volume is given in the last column of the table, and the entries are a derived view of the tabulated integrated cross sections. For the bins whose upper $x$ edge lies above $1$, only the range up to $x = 1$ enters the bin volume. The values are Born-level cross sections: they are corrected for detector effects and for radiative (QED and electroweak) effects; the correction convention is photon exchange only, i.e. the cross sections are defined without $Z$-boson exchange. Each cross section is quoted with its statistical uncertainty and its total systematic uncertainty. Two correction factors are tabulated for reference: the factor applied in this table (seventh column), which follows the photon-exchange-only convention, and the corresponding factor of the convention with $Z$-boson exchange included (sixth column); the ratio of the two factors converts a cross section between the two conventions. The tabulated entries are cross sections divided by the bin volume in $Q^2$, $x$, $z$ and $p_{T,h}$, in units of nb~GeV$^{-3}$; the bin volume is given in the last column of the table, and the entries are a derived view of the tabulated integrated cross sections. For the bins whose upper $x$ edge lies above $1$, only the range up to $x = 1$ enters the bin volume. The values are Born-level cross sections: they are corrected for detector effects and for radiative (QED and electroweak) effects; the correction convention is photon exchange only, i.e. the cross sections are defined without $Z$-boson exchange. Each cross section is quoted with its statistical uncertainty and its total systematic uncertainty. Two correction factors are tabulated for reference: the factor applied in this table (seventh column), which follows the photon-exchange-only convention, and the corresponding factor of the convention with $Z$-boson exchange included (sixth column); the ratio of the two factors converts a cross section between the two conventions. The tabulated entries are cross sections divided by the bin volume in $Q^2$, $x$, $z$ and $p_{T,h}$, in units of nb~GeV$^{-3}$; the bin volume is given in the last column of the table, and the entries are a derived view of the tabulated integrated cross sections. For the bins whose upper $x$ edge lies above $1$, only the range up to $x = 1$ enters the bin volume. The values are Born-level cross sections: they are corrected for detector effects and for radiative (QED and electroweak) effects; the correction convention is photon exchange only, i.e. the cross sections are defined without $Z$-boson exchange. Each cross section is quoted with its statistical uncertainty and its total systematic uncertainty. Two correction factors are tabulated for reference: the factor applied in this table (seventh column), which follows the photon-exchange-only convention, and the corresponding factor of the convention with $Z$-boson exchange included (sixth column); the ratio of the two factors converts a cross section between the two conventions. In this block the physical range of $x$ ends at $x = 1$; the bin volume given in the last column of the table uses this physical limit. The values are preliminary and subject to change.}
\label{tab:sidis-crosssections-noZ-neg-S3x0}
